description:
In this Bible Q&A episode, we explore the meaning behind some key passages: Mark 7:15–23, Philippians 2:5–7, and Matthew 4:1. Discover how these verses reveal powerful themes of purity, humility, and spiritual readiness—along with answers to other biblical questions—to help you grow in faith and understanding.


Send us your Bible Questions! 
By email: BibleQA@3abn.org 
By text: (618) 228-3975

QUESTIONS COVERED:

1. I was following a Bible reading on YouTube, and they said that pork and shrimp are not unclean to us because we are no longer under the curse. It says Jesus bore these curses on the cross, and under the New Covenant, we are free from the Mosaic Law. Can you explain Mark 7:15-23? 

2. Can you please explain Philippians 2:5-7? 

3.  I have noticed that I have trouble sleeping on Saturday nights. I believe this is due to not engaging in physical activity on the Sabbath. Do you have any suggestions on how I can overcome this unfortunate situation and still manage to keep the Sabbath day holy? What physical activities are acceptable on the Sabbath?

4. If Satan knows he will be defeated in the end, why does he not repent? 

5.  1 Samuel 31:4 says that Saul took a sword and fell on it. 2 Samuel 1:10 says, ”so I stood over him and killed him.” This is confusing. Did Saul kill himself or did the Amalekite kill him? 

6. Can you please explain Matthew 4:1? It says that the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. Does the Holy Spirit lead us into temptation? 

7. Why was such a detrimental act done to Ananias and Sapphira for lying to the Holy Spirit? Please help me to understand why they fell over and died. Why did Ananias and Sapphira die?

8. Can you give examples from the Bible on how it handles wine and whether it is ok to drink it? What does the Bible say about drinking wine?

9.  In the story of Job, where God allowed Satan to attack Job, was it God’s will for Satan to attack Job? Can you please explain the story of Job?

10.  Genesis 1:1 says, "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth." Then goes on to lay out day 1 to day 6 all that God had created, including His creation of man, and He rested on the 7th day. 2 Peter 3:8 says, "But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day." If one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, did it take God six thousand years to create Heaven and Earth? Then He rested one thousand years? 

11. Why do we need to pray for blessings? Wouldn't God automatically want to bless a church, ministry, or evangelistic meeting? What does my individual prayer do? 

12. Why does the book Song of Songs exist in the Bible? What is its purpose? How come no one talks about it?
